name: Audio amplifier ICs
summary: Amplifier chips that drive speakers, from tiny 0.5W parts to 100W class-D boards.
uses: Building a radio or PA amplifier
Driving a loud alarm or siren
identify: Chips on heatsinks near the speaker wires in stereos, TVs, computer speakers, car radios and Bluetooth speakers, marked LM386, TDA2030, TDA7297, TPA3116 or PAM8403.
test: Easiest to test in place: play sound from a phone into it and listen. A hot chip with no sound, or a loud hum, means it’s dead.
